problem.text: Let $N$ be the number of consecutive $0$'s at the right end of the decimal representation of the product $1!2!3!4!\cdots99!100!$. Find the remainder when $N$ is divided by $1000$.

steps.title: Where to start: count factors of $5$
steps.body: Each zero at the end of a number comes from one factor of $10 = 2 \cdot 5$. A product of factorials has far more factors of $2$ than factors of $5$, so the number of trailing zeros equals the number of factors of $5$ in the whole product.

your_turn.prompt: How many factors of $5$ are in $10!$?
your_turn.answer: Two: one from $5$ and one from $10$.

steps.title: Use Legendre's formula on each factorial
steps.body:
Legendre's formula says the number of $5$s in $n!$ is $\lfloor n/5 \rfloor + \lfloor n/25 \rfloor + \cdots$, where $\lfloor x \rfloor$ means round down. For $n \le 100$ only the first two terms matter, so we add up over all $n$ from $1$ to $100$:
$$N = \sum_{n=1}^{100} \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{5} \right\rfloor + \sum_{n=1}^{100} \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{25} \right\rfloor$$

your_turn.prompt: How many factors of $5$ does $100!$ alone contribute?

steps.title: The first sum: blocks of five
steps.body: $\lfloor n/5 \rfloor$ stays the same for five $n$ in a row: it is $0$ for $n = 1$ to $4$, $1$ for $n = 5$ to $9$, $2$ for $n = 10$ to $14$, and so on up to $19$ for $n = 95$ to $99$. Then $n = 100$ adds a single $20$. So the first sum is $5(1 + 2 + \cdots + 19) + 20$.

steps.title: The second sum: extra fives from multiples of $25$
steps.body: Careful: stopping at $970$ is the classic trap. Numbers like $25$ and $50$ carry two factors of $5$, and $\lfloor n/25 \rfloor$ counts the second one. It is $0$ for $n = 1$ to $24$, $1$ for the $25$ values $n = 25$ to $49$, $2$ for $n = 50$ to $74$, $3$ for $n = 75$ to $99$, and $4$ for $n = 100$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The total number of factors of $5$, and so the number of trailing zeros, is $N = 970 + 154 = 1124$. Dividing by $1000$ leaves remainder $124$. The answer is **124**.
